notes: Phase 3 gate: V1 text mode, the element channel alone (spec docs/specs/element-channel.md section 11, decision D7). First-rank 26.5% against the 0.236% chance reference, top-ten 80.0% against 2.36%, median rank 4 of 419-424 decoys, mean trial score 0.9797. Against the P2b sketch reference v1-dev-wit-99c8b508 (40.5% / 73.5% / median 2): text ranks fewer targets first but buries far fewer - 4 targets past rank 50 against 19 in sketch mode. Correspondence is established by level, not by correlation: the target's best-element similarity has median 0.4076 against 0.0802 across all 85,000 (submission, image) pairs, and 0 of 2,000 pairing permutations reach 0.4076. The named element comes from the target's own objects field in 84.1% of trials against a permutation baseline of 35.5%. Two caveats recorded, neither verdict-changing. (1) Corpus heterogeneity: the union index mixes 225 pool photographs with 200 inserted FS-COCO photographs and the highest-scoring decoy is an inserted photograph in 160 of 200 trials against a corpus-neutral 46.9%; 747 of the union's 2,274 element-bank entries occur only in the inserted photographs. Two attempts to restate the chance reference from a permutation null were refuted - the estimator is a function of the result it would divide, and stratifying by content similarity shows the same elevation for pool targets - so the recorded references stand and the P2b sketch record needs no revision. (2) Coverage: all 200 submissions produced exactly one atom, because the selected FS-COCO captions are single sentences with no commas, so this gate did not exercise inter-atom Sinkhorn competition, the reserve bin, or rarity discrimination between atoms. The reserve is structurally unreachable for a one-atom submission: the naming test reduces to a strictly positive centered cosine, and the report named an element in 200 of 200 rows. Fusion weights equal and unfitted (I6). Reproduced exactly: an independent rebuild matched decoy_count, beaten, tied, target_rank and p in 200 of 200 trials with zero provider requests.
